title: How to set up a content calendar that you stick to
description:
Buffer followed more than 100,000 accounts for 26 weeks. Accounts that posted in at least 20 of those weeks got over five times the engagement per post of accounts that posted in four weeks or fewer. So the calendar in this video is built around the week: pick the number of posts you can make every week, including the bad ones.

For a number, Buffer's study of 11.4 million TikTok posts points to 2 to 5 posts a week; start at the bottom of that range. The template is one row per post: date, platform, format, the idea, the content pillar (3 to 5 topics you keep coming back to) and a status (idea, draft, ready). Fill it in one sitting: Later puts a monthly planning session at 45 to 60 minutes, and Hootsuite says most teams plan one to four weeks ahead. Jade Beason's advice is to start by batching one week, on one platform. Keep a bank of ready posts for the weeks that fall apart: Buffer's best results came at 21 of 26 weeks, so a few weeks off still count.

The studies are correlational: consistent accounts may differ in other ways too.
